key_insight: Graph neural networks are most valuable when relational structure is genuinely informative, but their gains depend heavily on domain-specific graph construction, architecture choice, and the limits imposed by heterophily, scale, and temporal dynamics.
engineering_relevance: For practitioners, the main takeaway is to match the graph and model to the task rather than assume message passing will outperform non-graph baselines, especially in deployment settings with shift, robustness, or fairness constraints.
method: Unifies spectral and spatial GNN formulations under a shared design space.
Maps model expressiveness to the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy to clarify what architectures can and cannot distinguish.
Benchmarks twelve application domains by graph-construction cost, dominant architectures, and baseline quality.
evidence_signal: The survey compares reported results across twelve domains and explicitly checks whether gains are robust or explained by weak baselines, favorable splits, or deployment mismatches.
watch_item: Temporal, heterophilous, and large-scale graphs remain difficult, and leaderboard performance may not translate to real-world deployment.
paper_title: Graph Neural Networks Applications Across Domains: All Insights You Need
